title: Confabulation — your brain invents memories every single day
voiceover: Your brain is a liar. Every time you remember something, you don't replay it. You rebuild it from fragments. And every time you rebuild it, you change it a little. Filling in details that were never there. Smoothing over gaps. This is called confabulation. In experiments, scientists have implanted entirely false memories in people — convincing them they got lost in a mall as a child when they never did — and the subjects later described the event in vivid detail. They felt the fear. Heard their mother's voice. Saw the strangers around them. None of it happened. You are a story your brain tells itself. Follow Mindbloom for one fact a day.
